clue.text: Entertainment where cola is served

indicators.note: a ball served in tennis is sent somewhere new, so these letters are dished out in a fresh order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A party where soft drinks are handed round to guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering, a kind of entertainment laid on for a group.

clue.text: Reserves in sight when bus turns up on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the vehicle, written backwards
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A footballer spots the substitutes arriving by coach for a Sunday match.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts the Sunday letter below the bus, i.e. after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Subs is short for substitutes, the reserve players waiting on the bench.

clue.text: Most musclemen need time to be merciful

indicators.note: only most of the word is wanted, so its opening letters are dropped and the larger part kept

parts.note: the word whose final six letters are kept
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Bodybuilders mostly need time off to soften up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' here takes the last six of nine letters, dropping MUS from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement describes someone lenient who shows mercy, as in clemency.

clue.text: Line dances not starting to strain

indicators.note: the word must lose its opening letter before it is used

parts.note: the word that loses its first letter
to try is to strain or test, as in trying one's patience

explanation.surface: Line dancers struggle to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line dances' reads as one phrase, but 'Line' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Line in the sense of lineage or descent from forebears is a synonym for ancestry.

clue.text: Plans to reform team with cash

indicators.note: reforming something remakes it in a new shape, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A club owner's plans to rebuild the side by spending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemata is the plural of schema, an outline plan or diagrammatic scheme.

clue.text: Possible telegram with contents: 'After four o'clock'

indicators.note: a message with contents holds something inside it, so the following words go within

parts.note: a cable is an old word for a telegram
once means after, as in 'once you have eaten'
four as it appears in Roman numerals on a clock face

explanation.surface: A telegram that merely says 'After four o'clock' could mean anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the words look like a message; they are the letters packed inside the telegram, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conceivable can be imagined, so it is possible.

clue.text: Snowed, moving leaves

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so these letters change places

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Snow is falling and the autumn leaves are blowing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb, as in leaving money in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give or bequeath property, so leaves in the will sense matches.

clue.text: Protein needed for bum damaged with nail

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A backside injured by a nail needs protein to heal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum is British slang for the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumin is a water-soluble protein found in egg white and blood plasma.

clue.text: Mountains make a writer take a size larger than eights!

parts.note: taken as written
a pen is a writing instrument
the next size up from eights

explanation.surface: A writer outgrowing their clothes needs bigger sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: My brother is drawn to every quarrel

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brother; 'My' is surface dressing
each and every mean the same

explanation.surface: Someone complains their brother gets pulled into every row.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a rift or falling-out between people, a quarrel.

clue.text: I study, turning to Bible (no intro), which is unpalatable

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning the word round means reading its letters from the end

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: with no introduction the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the word that loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns to scripture study and finds it hard to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a verb but is the noun for a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food is not fit to eat, and unpalatable describes food unpleasant to eat.

clue.text: Lady perhaps often found between folded sheets

definitions.text: Lady perhaps often found between folded sheets

parts.words: Lady perhaps often found between folded sheets
parts.note: surface reading: a woman tucked up in bed between the sheets
setter's reading: the folded sheets are the pages of a daily paper, where a female journalist's work and byline appear

explanation.surface: A lady who is often to be found in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bedclothes picture misleads; the sheets are newsprint folded into an edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A female journalist works for a daily paper, so her name appears between its folded pages.

clue.text: A short note admits name of first girl to kiss men in triumph

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them inside, so what follows goes within the note

parts.note: taken as written
a chit is a brief written note
Eve was the first woman in Genesis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brief letter confesses that the first girl kissed the men in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to kiss' means touching, so the girl's name sits right beside the men inside the note.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement is something accomplished successfully, a triumph or feat.

clue.text: Pudding to enjoy, so a bloke gets it all round his face

definitions.text: so a bloke gets it all round his face

parts.note: afters is British slang for the dessert course of a meal
to have can mean to enjoy, as in having a good time

explanation.surface: A man eats dessert so messily it ends up all over his face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures pudding smeared on a face; the definition is the lotion a man pats on after shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is the scented lotion men splash on their cheeks and chin after a shave.

clue.text: Refrained from dishonour in any bed

parts.note: the article a can mean any, as in 'a child could do it'

indicators.note: the first word is placed in the middle of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written
a stain on one's character is a dishonour

explanation.surface: Someone avoided disgrace by not sleeping in just any bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain deliberately, especially from drinking, voting or indulgence.

clue.text: Writer may be unknown, but the front of the canon is missing

indicators.note: points at the opening letter of the word that follows as the one to go
something missing has been taken away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the word that loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A literary note: some author is anonymous, and the start of the canon is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, is printed in place of the author's name when the writer is not known.

clue.text: Tavern — a hole converted to cash in on

indicators.note: a building that is converted is remodelled, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
to cash in on something is to use it for gain

explanation.surface: A developer turns a dump into a pub to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a pub or tavern selling beer.

clue.text: To knock back lager is a mistake

indicators.note: to knock something back sends it the other way, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: Pils is a pale lager, short for Pilsner

explanation.surface: Downing lager is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like drinking, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error, as in a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Be left at home with mother (Italian in part)

parts.note: being in means being at home
a mother is a her, a female
IT is the short form of Italian, a part of the word

explanation.surface: Someone stays at home with their part-Italian mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be left' is passive: when something is left to you in a will, you come into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property bequeathed by someone who has died, to be left it.

clue.text: Dealers in medicinal plants wearing shirts able to be repaired

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, here with its letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plant sellers dressed in shirts that could be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbalists prepare and sell herbal remedies made from medicinal plants.

clue.text: Man's cut dreadfully, needing a private room

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is badly botched, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man has been badly wounded and needs somewhere private to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a secluded private retreat, a room where one is free from intrusion.

clue.text: A pie's made up of several layers

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
a tart is a pie, with the 's adding a final letter

explanation.surface: A pie built up from several layers of pastry and filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like 'composed', but in a down clue it puts the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, especially of rock or sediment, one upon another.

clue.text: A gift from the king of Siam, but quite useless

definitions.text: A gift from the king of Siam
definitions.meaning: first meaning: kings of Siam reputedly gave a sacred pale beast to courtiers they wished to ruin with its upkeep
second meaning: a possession that is costly and of no practical use

explanation.walkthrough: Siam is the old name for Thailand; the costly royal gift is the origin of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a burdensome, useless possession, from the legend of the royal Siamese present that bankrupted its keeper.

clue.text: Smile broadly, but the laborious routine never ends

indicators.note: a routine that never reaches its end loses its last letter

parts.note: the grind is tedious, laborious work

explanation.surface: Keep smiling, even though the daily slog goes on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin is to smile widely, showing the teeth.

clue.text: Details put back in preset arrangements

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the letters run from the end
the letters needed sit inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Specifics are restored to arrangements made in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Details' looks like a noun but is the verb: to detail is to recount.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail something is to describe it fully, as one narrates a story.

clue.text: I'm parking here to speak in this club

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: A member announces they have parked and will address the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society; it is a golf club used on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used for gentle strokes on the green.

clue.text: Spoils of holy man getting transported back

indicators.note: going back means the whole string is read from its end

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
carted means carried or transported

explanation.surface: A saint's plunder is carried off home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like loot but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that detracts from a thing lessens its value or appeal, so it spoils it.

clue.text: Sailors in the southeast must have the last word

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
amen ends a prayer, so it is the last word

explanation.surface: Sailors from the southeast insist on having the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are sailors, people who work at sea.
